proposals.before: Pei Du, taboo name Zhongli, was a man of Wenxi in Hedong.
proposals.after: Pei Du, courtesy name Zhongli, was a man of Wenxi in Hedong.
proposals.reason: 字 marks a courtesy name (style), not a taboo/personal avoidance name; the idiomatic correctly has styled Zhongli.

proposals.before: Recommended as outstanding in the Filial and Incorrupt, Upright and Learned examination, he was assigned as magistrate of Heyin.
proposals.after: Recommended as outstanding in the Worthy and Upright examination, he was assigned as magistrate of Heyin.
proposals.reason: 賢良方正 is the Worthy and Upright decree examination, not the Filial and Incorrupt (孝廉) category.

proposals.before: He was nominated as exceptionally qualified in the Filial and Incorrupt, Upright and Learned category, and was transferred to be magistrate of Heyin.
proposals.after: He was nominated as exceptionally qualified in the Worthy and Upright category, and was transferred to be magistrate of Heyin.
proposals.reason: Same error as the idiomatic: 賢良方正 should not be rendered as Filial and Incorrupt.

proposals.before: When his illness was cured, he was ordered not to need the Xuanzheng Yamen but to answer directly at Yanying, and was appointed vice director of the Central Secretariat and Associate Director of the Chancellery.
proposals.after: When his illness was cured, he was ordered not to need the Xuanzheng Yamen but to answer directly at Yanying, and was appointed vice director of the Central Secretariat and jointly manager of affairs with the Secretariat-Chancellery.
proposals.reason: 同中書門下平章事 is associate chief minister / joint manager of affairs, not Associate Director of the Chancellery.

proposals.before: Du remonstrated, "Since Wang E's death there have already been several accusations.
proposals.after: Du remonstrated, "Since Wang E's death there have already been several offerings.
proposals.reason: 獻 here means tributary offerings or presentations of wealth, not accusations; the literal correctly has submissions.

proposals.before: Feng Ji had long resented Du, and the emperor, weary of obstruction at court, was glad to send him to the front.
proposals.after: Feng Ji had long resented Du; the emperor, weary of obstruction at court, sent Feng Ji away from the center.
proposals.reason: Chinese 出之外 refers to removing Feng Ji from court, not sending Pei Du to the front; Du's departure was already arranged in prior units.

proposals.before: Before long Li Su stormed Xuanchi by night and sent word that Wu Yuanji had been captured.
proposals.after: Before long Li Su entered Xuanhu by night and sent word that Wu Yuanji had been captured.
proposals.reason: 懸瓠 is Xuanhu (the Cai stronghold), not Xuanchi; the idiomatic place-name is a mistransliteration.

proposals.before: Rewarded for his service, he was promoted to Grand Master of Splendid Happiness with Golden Seal and Purple Ribbon, Hanlin academician of the Hongwen Hall, Supreme Pillar of the State, and Duke of Jin with three thousand households, and restored to the chancellorship.
proposals.after: Rewarded for his service, he was promoted to Grand Master of Splendid Happiness with Golden Seal and Purple Ribbon, Grand Academician of the Hongwen Hall, Supreme Pillar of the State, and Duke of Jin with three thousand households, and restored to the chancellorship.
proposals.reason: 弘文館大學士 is Grand Academician of the Hongwen Hall, not a Hanlin academician.

proposals.before: For his merit in planning he was advanced to Grand Master of Splendid Happiness with Golden Seal and Purple Ribbon, Hanlin academician of the Hongwen Hall, Supreme Pillar of the State, Duke of Jin with three thousand households, and again put in charge of government affairs.
proposals.after: For recorded meritorious service he was advanced to Grand Master of Splendid Happiness with Golden Seal and Purple Ribbon, Grand Academician of the Hongwen Hall, Supreme Pillar of the State, Duke of Jin with three thousand households, and again put in charge of government affairs.
proposals.reason: 策勳 means evaluating/recording merit for reward, not 'merit in planning'; 弘文館大學士 is not Hanlin.

proposals.before: It would be better to nurture prestige north of the Yellow River, wait until frost falls and waters subside, cut off Yangliu, press deep to Yun, and encamp at Yanggu—then every man will fight to a different death and the rebels' power will be exhausted."
proposals.after: It would be better to nurture prestige north of the Yellow River, wait until frost falls and waters subside, cut off Yangliu, press deep to Yun, and encamp at Yanggu—then every man will fight to the death and the rebels' power will be exhausted."
proposals.reason: 殊死 means fight to the death, not 'fight to a different death'.

proposals.before: '" The emperor said, "Excellent."
proposals.after: The emperor said, "Excellent."
proposals.reason: Leading corrupted quote marks are bleed from the previous sentence and are not part of the English.

proposals.before: '" The emperor said: "Good."
proposals.after: The emperor said: "Good."
proposals.reason: Leading corrupted quote marks are bleed from the previous sentence and are not part of the English.

proposals.before: The great merchant Zhang Zhi owed interest money to the Five Wards; the emperor ordered Ward envoy Yang Chaowen to seize his household registers. Examining loans, though they had already been repaid, all were hooked and stopped; tracing back, several tens and hundreds of people were implicated, lined up with cudgels and staffs to coerce non-confession.
proposals.after: The great merchant Zhang Zhi owed interest money to the Five Wards; the emperor ordered Ward envoy Yang Chaowen to seize his household registers. Examining loans, though they had already been repaid, all were hooked and stopped; tracing back, several tens and hundreds of people were implicated, lined up with cudgels and staffs and coerced until they confessed.
proposals.reason: 脅不承 describes coercion of people who would not confess, i.e. beating them into confession, not 'coerce non-confession' as the outcome.

proposals.before: Tan appealed on his son's behalf. Chaowen answered evasively, "The money went into the inner palace. How can it be recovered?"
proposals.after: Tan's son appealed upward. Chaowen answered evasively, "The money went into the inner palace. How can it be recovered?"
proposals.reason: Chinese 坦子上訴 means Tan's son appealed, not that Tan appealed on his son's behalf.

proposals.before: Before long Yuan Zhen was made chief minister anyway, while Du was left as acting Minister of Works, grand councillor in name only, and regent of the eastern capital.
proposals.after: Before long Yuan Zhen was made chief minister anyway, while Du was left as acting Minister of Works, grand councillor, and regent of the eastern capital.
proposals.reason: Chinese 平章事 does not say the councillorship was in name only; that gloss invents a qualifier absent from the source.

proposals.before: The emperor said: "I did not reach knowing.
proposals.after: The emperor said: "I did not come to know of it.
proposals.reason: Literal calque of 我不及知 is unintelligible English; the sense is that the emperor was not informed.

proposals.before: Moreover your servant views the heavenly countenance not a foot away—just now he still could not decide; a thousand li away with a single word, could Wu reach the sage ear?"
proposals.after: Moreover your servant views the heavenly countenance not a foot away—just now he still could not decide; a thousand li away with a single word, could it awaken the sage ear?"
proposals.reason: In 可悟聖聽哉 the verb 悟 means awaken/reach, not the person Liu Wu; the literal wrongly turns the verb into a personal name.

proposals.before: Your Majesty sighs at table, lamenting the lack of men like Xiao He and Cao Shen. Yet Pei Du alone has been cast aside. This is why Feng Tang knew that Emperor Wen of Han possessed generals like Li Guang and Wei Qing yet could not use them."
proposals.after: Your Majesty sighs at table, lamenting the lack of men like Xiao He and Cao Shen. Yet Pei Du alone has been cast aside. This is why Feng Tang knew that Emperor Wen of Han possessed generals like Lian Po and Li Mu yet could not use them."
proposals.reason: Chinese 頗、牧 are Lian Po (廉頗) and Li Mu (李牧) in the Feng Tang–Emperor Wen anecdote; Li Guang and Wei Qing are a mistranslation.

proposals.before: Your Majesty at meals sighs, regretting there are no Xiao He or Cao Shen; now a single Pei Du is cast aside outside—this is why Feng Tang knew that Emperor Wen of Han had Li Guang and Wei Qing yet could not employ them."
proposals.after: Your Majesty at meals sighs, regretting there are no Xiao He or Cao Shen; now a single Pei Du is cast aside outside—this is why Feng Tang knew that Emperor Wen of Han had Lian Po and Li Mu yet could not employ them."
proposals.reason: Chinese 頗、牧 denote Lian Po and Li Mu, not Li Guang and Wei Qing.

proposals.before: Zhu Kerong seized imperial-gift-robes envoy Yang Wenduan, falsely claiming he had slighted him, and also complained that what was bestowed was excessive and vile; he further begged to borrow three hundred thousand bolts of cloth from the treasury, otherwise the army would surely mutiny;
proposals.after: Zhu Kerong seized imperial-gift-robes envoy Yang Wenduan, falsely claiming he had slighted him, and also complained that what was bestowed was shoddy and inferior; he further begged to borrow three hundred thousand bolts of cloth from the treasury, otherwise the army would surely mutiny;
proposals.reason: 濫惡 means gifts of poor/shoddy quality, not 'excessive and vile'; the idiomatic rendering already has 'shoddy'.

proposals.before: Du declined exemption from investiture rites.
proposals.after: Du declined the investiture rites.
proposals.reason: Chinese 讓免冊禮 means he asked to forgo the investiture ceremony, not that he declined an exemption.

proposals.before: He was posthumously made Grand Tutor with the posthumous name Wenzong. Funeral gifts were lavish, and Capital Intendant Zheng Fu was ordered to oversee the rites.
proposals.after: He was posthumously made Grand Tutor with the posthumous name Wenzhong. Funeral gifts were lavish, and Capital Intendant Zheng Fu was ordered to oversee the rites.
proposals.reason: Chinese 諡文忠 is Wenzhong; Wenzong is the emperor temple name and is wrong here.

proposals.before: By patent he was posthumously made Grand Tutor, posthumous name Wenzong, funeral gifts lavish and detailed; Capital Metropolis Intendant Zheng Fu was ordered to oversee the funeral.
proposals.after: By patent he was posthumously made Grand Tutor, posthumous name Wenzhong, funeral gifts lavish and detailed; Capital Metropolis Intendant Zheng Fu was ordered to oversee the funeral.
proposals.reason: Chinese 文忠 must be Wenzhong, not Wenzong.

proposals.before: Shi, taboo name Tongli, was by nature keen and perceptive; whatever passed his eyes he never forgot.
proposals.after: Shi, courtesy name Tongli, was by nature keen and perceptive; whatever passed his eyes he never forgot.
proposals.reason: Chinese 字 marks a courtesy name, not a taboo personal name.

proposals.before: Emperor Xuanzong chose renowned ministers: Shi for Jingyuan, Bi Dan for Bin-Ning, and Li Fu for Xiazhou, and saw them off in person.
proposals.after: Emperor Xuanzong chose renowned ministers: Shi to command Jingyuan, Bi Dan to command Bin-Ning, and Li Fu to command Xiazhou, and saw them off in person.
proposals.reason: Chinese 帥 means to command each circuit; the idiomatic English omits the command verb and reads as if the men themselves were the place assignments.

proposals.before: Shi with them established garrison limits—when full, replace;
proposals.after: Shi established garrison term limits—when a tour was complete, replace;
proposals.reason: 與立 here means establishing the limits, not 'with them'; the current literal invents a companion reading and is ungrammatical English.

proposals.before: He gave him fruit from the imperial casket. Shen knelt and received it with both hands.
proposals.after: He gave him fruit from the imperial casket. Shen raised his robe and knelt to receive it.
proposals.reason: Chinese 舉衣跽受 is raising the robe and kneeling to receive; the idiomatic invents 'with both hands' and drops 舉衣.

proposals.before: The hard part was not defeating the rebels but entrusting Du to do it.
proposals.after: It was not Du's defeating the rebels that was difficult—it was entrusting Du that was difficult.
proposals.reason: Chinese repeats 度 in both clauses (非度破賊之難，任度之為難); the idiomatic drops the first Du and flattens the parallel.

decisions.reason: Chinese 字中立 marks a courtesy name (style); 諱 would be a taboo name. Replacing “taboo name” with “courtesy name” matches the source and the idiomatic “styled Zhongli.”
賢良方正 is the Worthy and Upright decree examination; Filial and Incorrupt is 孝廉, a different category. The proposed wording restores the correct exam name.
Same source as the idiomatic line: 賢良方正 is Worthy and Upright, not Filial and Incorrupt (孝廉).

同中書門下平章事 is the chancellorial title “jointly manager of affairs with the Secretariat-Chancellery,” not Associate Director of the Chancellery; the repair matches the Chinese office formula and the idiomatic associate-chief-minister sense.
數有獻 means there had been several offerings/presentations of wealth after Wang E’s death; 獻 is not “accusations.” Context 冒遺獻 confirms the submission/offering sense.
Subject of 出之外 is Feng Ji: 逢吉忌度，帝惡居中撓沮，出之外. Prior units already send Du to the front; this flashback removes Feng Ji from the center, so “send him to the front” misattributes the pronoun.

sourceWitness.excerpt: 逢吉忌度，帝惡居中撓沮，出之外

decisions.reason: 懸瓠 is Xuanhu, the Cai stronghold; Xuanchi is a mistransliteration. 夜入 also supports “entered” over “stormed.”
弘文館大學士 is Grand Academician of the Hongwen Hall; Hanlin (翰林) is a different office and is not in the Chinese.
策勳 means recording/evaluating merit for reward, not “merit in planning,” and 弘文館大學士 is Grand Academician of the Hongwen Hall, not a Hanlin academician.
殊死 means fighting to the death; “fight to a different death” is a calque of 殊 that invents a wrong sense.
Leading '" marks are bleed from the previous sentence’s closing quotation and are not part of 上曰：「善。」
Same bleed of closing quote marks into this unit; the Chinese begins cleanly with 上曰.
列箠挺脅不承 describes lining people up and coercing those who would not confess—i.e. beating them into confession—not producing “non-confession” as the outcome.
坦子上訴 means Tan’s son appealed upward; the original reverses agent and beneficiary by making Tan the appellant on his son’s behalf.
Chinese 平章事 states the office without any “in name only” qualifier; that gloss invents a limitation absent from the source.

sourceWitness.excerpt: 守司空、平章事、東都留守

decisions.reason: 我不及知 means the emperor had not been informed / did not come to know of it; “I did not reach knowing” is an unintelligible calque.
In 可悟聖聽哉, 悟 is the verb “awaken/reach” governing 聖聽, not the person Liu Wu; turning it into “could Wu reach” invents personal-name attribution.
頗、牧 in the Feng Tang–Emperor Wen anecdote are Lian Po (廉頗) and Li Mu (李牧); Li Guang and Wei Qing are unrelated generals and misidentify the allusion.
Same Chinese 頗、牧: Lian Po and Li Mu, not Li Guang and Wei Qing.
所賜濫惡 complains that the bestowed gifts were shoddy/inferior in quality; “excessive and vile” misreads 濫惡.
讓免冊禮 means he asked to forgo / declined the investiture ceremony; “declined exemption from” reverses the sense into refusing an exemption.
諡文忠 is the posthumous name Wenzhong; Wenzong (文宗) is an emperor temple name and is not what 文忠 says.
Chinese 文忠 must be romanized Wenzhong, not Wenzong.
字通理 marks a courtesy name; “taboo name” would require 諱 and is incorrect here.
以識帥涇原…畢諴帥邠甯…李福帥夏州 uses 帥 “to command” for each posting; “Shi for Jingyuan” omits that verb and flattens the appointments.

sourceWitness.excerpt: 以識帥涇原，畢諴帥邠甯，李福帥夏州

decisions.reason: 識與立戍限 means Shi established garrison term limits; reading 與 as “with them” invents companions and yields ungrammatical English.
舉衣跽受 is raising the robe and kneeling to receive; “with both hands” invents a gesture and drops 舉衣.
非度破賊之難，任度之為難也 repeats 度 in both clauses; the original drops the first Du and flattens the parallel contrast the historian draws.
